subject: BrightHealth pilot: connection scaling checklist & rate-cap next steps
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: samir.patel@brighthealth.ai
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: BrightHealth pilot: connection scaling checklist & rate-cap next steps

Samir / Meera (looping you via reply),

Thanks again for the call earlier — quick recap and an action checklist so we can scope the pilot. Below are the performance SLOs and concurrency details we captured; please confirm or correct anything in-line.

Key SLOs you described:
- Target p95 latency for short prompts (<=256 tokens): 200ms
- Sustained throughput target: ~450 requests/sec for the model path used in the demo
- Peak concurrency observed in your simulated load: ~120 parallel "active" requests (requests that keep a socket open while streaming)
- Streaming sessions: 30-60 concurrent streams on average, occasional spikes to ~90 for short bursts

Concurrency & connection model notes (our read):
- You prefer connection pooling from your edge (reuse TCP + TLS keepalive) rather than opening new sockets per request.
- HTTP/2 multiplexing vs long-lived HTTP/1.1 keepalive: you currently use HTTP/1.1 with a custom pool; interested in switching to HTTP/2 if it reduces socket count.
- KV cache & prompt warmup: many of your requests share prefixes; prefix caching should reduce token cost once streaming is established.

Redwood initial rate/quota proposal (starting point for pilot):
- Per-tenant baseline QPS: 500 req/s (sustained) with auto-scaling headroom to 800 for short bursts
- Connection pool guidance: 250 client-side pooled connections; allow 1.5x multiplexing headroom on our side to accommodate long-poll/stream behavior
- Concurrency window: reserved 150 concurrent active sessions; burst tokens of 300 requests over a 60s window for startup spikes

Attachments: I attached the short checklist + topology diagram for your engineering review: brighthealth_concurrency_requirements_v1.pdf, conn_pool_topology.png

Next steps
- Samir/Meera: confirm the numbers above (latency & concurrency). Also add any long-stream use cases (duration > 60s).
- From our side: Aditya will follow up with a brief ops note on connection pooling recommendations and a draft ratecard for the pilot.
- If everything looks good, we can lock the pilot capacity and spin up a dedicated namespace for the POC next week.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions PM | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@brighthealth.ai>

Cc: meera.k@brighthealth.ai, pilot-ops@brighthealth.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:28:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: BrightHealth pilot: connection scaling checklist & rate-cap next steps

Neha, thanks for the thorough recap. A few inline clarifications below.

> Target p95 latency for short prompts (<=256 tokens): 200ms
We still consider 200ms ambitious for sustained 450 QPS — acceptable as a goal for the demo path. If you can provide p99 breakdown that would help set expectations.

> Sustained throughput target: ~450 requests/sec
Confirm. Some of our traffic is bursty (end-of-day reports). Expect a 3-4x spike profile for ~90s each day.

> Peak concurrency observed: ~120 parallel active requests
Correct. Important note: about 20% of those keep a stream open for >75s (clinical transcript sessions).

Questions for Redwood (please reply):
1) Does Redwood's connection pooling assume HTTP/2 multiplexing or do you recommend keeping our existing HTTP/1.1 pool and increasing socket count?
2) For the burst profile (3-4x for 90s), what does your suggested burst token policy look like?
3) For pilot billing, we need a simple estimate of expected token cost vs. reserved capacity cost. Procurement will need that for the SOW.

We'll also loop procurement on the next thread once we align on the pilot footprint.

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Engineering | BrightHealth
samir.patel@brighthealth.ai
[Quoted-by: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com> from Wed, 09 Dec 2026 16:02:00 -0800]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: samir.patel@brighthealth.ai, meera.k@brighthealth.ai
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: BrightHealth pilot: connection scaling checklist & rate-cap next steps

Samir / Meera — quick technical responses inline and an ops recommendation.

1) HTTP/2 vs HTTP/1.1 pooling- We support both. If you can move to HTTP/2, multiplexing reduces TCP/TLS overhead and is preferable for lots of short concurrent streams. For long-lived streaming sessions (\u003e60s) HTTP/2 also helps by sharing connections. If migration is not feasible, increasing the HTTP/1.1 pool works too — we suggest keeping socket idle timeouts aligned (60s keepalive) to avoid churn.

2) Burst token policy (recommended)- Pilot config suggestion:
  - Sustained: 500 req/s per tenant
  - Burst: 3x sustained for up to 120s (so 1500 req/s allowable for 120s) governed by a token bucket (tokens refilled at sustained rate)
  - Concurrency reservation: 150 active sessions reserved; additional ephemeral concurrency allowed up to 320 if burst tokens remain

3) Billing & pilot estimate- Attached is a draft ratecard that maps expected token usage to an estimated monthly cost for the pilot and a reserved-capacity scenario. For a 30-day pilot with avg 450 req/s and our conservative tokenization assumptions (avg 35 tokens/request), ballpark token cost is in the attached ratecard (redwood_ratecard_draft.xlsx). We'll produce a short appendix for procurement explaining reserved vs on-demand tradeoffs.

Operational best practices for the pilot:
- Client-side: set a connection pool size matching expected concurrent streams/2 (so ~120 concurrent active -> pool of 60 per edge instance) and enable connection reuse across worker threads.
- Server-side (Redwood): we will provision a dedicated namespace with auto-scaling and a holding quota for 150 reserved concurrents and a burst policy as above.
- Monitoring: Neha will set up a dashboard (latency p50/p95/p99, active streams, socket count, error rate) and a daily sync for the first 5 days.

Let us know if we should tighten the burst window or concurrency reservation.

-Aditya

Aditya / Neha — this looks good and answers the majority of our questions. A few quick items before procurement gets involved:

- We will try a short HTTP/2 pilot on one edge region to measure socket reduction. If that looks stable, we'll move the rest of traffic over.
- Burst policy (3x sustained for 120s) aligns with our internal ops expectations. We may ask for a short spike increase in the first week of pilot for validation.
- Procurement asked for the token estimate and the draft ratecard; they should be able to review the attached spreadsheet and come back with SOW questions.

Next step: Neha, can you schedule a 30-minute ops sync Monday to confirm the namespace provisioning and a contact list for daily check-ins? Procurement (cc) — please advise on preferred SOW cadence.

Thanks,
Samir
